# Joseph and Aseneth Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS | **Section:** Joseph Refuses to Kiss Aseneth

---

**1** Aseneth came downstairs and stood before her parents. They took one look at her and were overwhelmed by her beauty, filled with joy.

**2** Pentephres said to Joseph: "This is our daughter Aseneth — the one I told you about. Come and greet her; she's like a sister to you." Joseph looked at her and felt something stir in him.

**3** Pentephres said to Aseneth: "Go greet your brother Joseph and give him a kiss." She walked toward Joseph to kiss him.

**4** But Joseph put out his right hand and held it against her chest, stopping her. He said: "A man who worships God — who blesses the living God with his lips, who eats the bread of life and drinks the cup of immortality and is anointed with the oil of incorruption — such a man cannot kiss a woman who worships dead, speechless idols, who eats at their altars the bread of death, who drinks from their offerings the cup of treachery, and who is smeared with the ointment of corruption.

**5** A man who worships God will kiss his mother, his sister, his kinswoman, his wife — women who also bless the living God with their mouths.

**6** In the same way, a woman who worships God should not kiss a man who is outside her faith. That is an abomination before the Lord God."

**7** Aseneth's face crumpled. She was cut to the heart by Joseph's words, and tears came to her eyes as she stared at him.

**8** When Joseph saw her, he felt a wave of compassion — he was gentle and kind and deeply God-fearing — and he reached out and put his right hand on her head.

**9** He prayed: "Lord God of my father Israel, Most High, Almighty, the one who gives life to everything, who calls people from darkness into light, from error into truth, from death into life — Lord, bless this young woman. Renew her by your Spirit. Remake her with your invisible hand. Give her life with your own life.

**10** Let her eat the bread of life and drink the cup of blessing, and count her among your people, those you chose before the world began."

**11** When Joseph finished praying, Aseneth felt a surge of joy. She ran upstairs and collapsed on her bed, spent — overcome with joy and grief and fear and trembling and tears all at once.

**12** After dinner, Joseph told Pentephres: "I need to start early tomorrow." Pentephres urged him: "Stay one more day — leave in the morning." Joseph held firm. "I have to go today. This is the day God has set my journey in motion. But if God is willing, I'll stop here on my way back and spend time with you."

---
*PNEUMA: modern English; verse-only numbering.*
